authContext.note: No explicit gate check (e.g. creatorGates()) or session read appears in either file in scope. requiresAuth is inferred only from the nature of the data (getCacBusinessRecord() returns 'the applicant's OWN CAC-registered business' with no id param, implying it is resolved server-side from the caller's identity) — not from any visible auth guard in these two files.

special.uploadsNote: Step 2 ('Documents') presents two upload affordances: 'Product sample photos' (pre-seeded as already 'uploading' on mount) and 'Bank reference letter' (user-triggered via 'Take a photo' / 'Choose file' buttons, doc key reference_letter). Neither calls any function in services.ts or mocks/services.ts — both are pure client-side timers (setInterval/setTimeout) that flip local DocSlot state from empty/uploading to uploaded with a fabricated progress percentage and filename. This is STUB-7 in stubs.json: no real upload endpoint exists or is seam-tagged anywhere for either document. A backend needs a presigned-upload-style endpoint for both documents that this screen currently has no contract for at all.

uiStatesDesigned.note: Same generic 'live service detail' pattern reused for both CAC and NEPC, but the frame's literal content is CAC's ('How it goes': Apply/Review/Access, StatBlocks for price+turnaround, 'What you get' checklist). The actual services-nepc/page.tsx code renders different copy (a custom 'How it works' 3-step list: 'Tell us what you make' / 'Share where you sell' / 'Talk to the export desk') and omits the StatBlock price/turnaround row and the 'What you get' checklist entirely — so this is the closest matching design frame by structure, not a literal match by content.
